content.title: Masters Par 3 Contest: Unfortunately for Aaron Rai, he won
content.text: AUGUSTA, Ga. — After two holes of the Masters Par 3 Contest, Justin Thomas sat at 3-under par. A birdie at No. 1 followed by a hole-in-one at No. 2 vaulted him to the top of the leaderboard … which is the last place an aspiring Masters winner wants to be.Famously, in the 63 times the contest has taken place in its traditional Wednesday slot ahead of the Masters, no player who has won the Par 3 has gone on to claim the green jacket four days later.AdvertisementOf those 63 winners, 21 have missed the cut, while just 10 have finished inside the top 10. Two have finished runner-up, with Raymond Floyd losing to Nick Faldo in a playoff in 1990.The last five Par 3 winners have gone on to finish 51, T30, Cut, T50/Cut, Cut.In fact, only two players — Ben Crenshaw and Vijay Singh — have won the Masters after winning the Par 3 Contest. Crenshaw won the Par 3 in 1987, then claimed his second green jacket in 1995. Singh won the Par 3 in 1994, then the Masters in 2000.At some point someone will win both in the same year, but Thomas apparently wasn’t interested in testing those waters. By hole 3, his name had fallen all the way to the bottom of the leaderboard, with a “WD” next to it. Whether by design or accident, Thomas had taken himself out of the competition, which can happen if a player lets someone hit for him — typically a spouse or child.AdvertisementAnd so Thomas’ hole-in-one …… was reduced to nothing more than a highlight.And he was hardly alone. Of the 80 players who entered the event, 63 did not post a score. This list includes: Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy, Bryson DeChambeau, Ludvig Åberg and Jon Rahm — aka the favorites.The Par 3 curse did not sway Aaron Rai. The two-glove wearing Englishman carded a 6-under 21 on his 9-hole round to win by a stroke.Rai, who made his Masters debut a year ago when he finished T27, currently has +20000 odds to win.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest updates and highlights from the 2026 Masters Par 3 contest:Live coverage is over20 updatesWed, April 8, 2026 at 3:37 PM CDTYahoo Sports StaffAaron Rai walks away with a win in the 2026 Masters Par 3 contest with a score of -6. After notching a birdie on the eighth hole, Im needed an ace on the final hole to tie things up. That didn’t happen.With Im out of the competition, Nick Taylor remains the biggest threat to Rai. Taylor sits at -3 through six holes, so it’s possible he puts the pressure on down the stretch.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 2:27 PM CDTChris CwikWe have our fourth ace at the 2026 Par 3 Contest. After seeing Justin Thomas, Wyndham Clark and Keegan Bradley get in on the act earlier, Tommy Fleetwood decided to join the group before the event ended.Fleetwood managed the feat on the fourth hole of the day.With his ace, that brings the total at the 2026 Par 3 Contest up to four, exceeding last year’s total of three aces.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 2:16 PM CDTChris CwikWith a possible win on the line, Aaron Rai delivered. He birdied his final hole of the day, taking a one-stroke lead over Jacob Bridgeman at the top of the leaderboard.Rai will now wait it out to see if anyone can catch him. But with most golfers back multiple strokes, that could prove difficult, as most players only have one or two holes left.Rai finished at -6 on the day.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 2:05 PM CDTChris CwikJacob Bridgeman shot -5 on the day in the Par 3 Contest. That performance was good enough to have Bridgeman finish the event in the lead.But it might not stay that way. Aaron Rai is tied with Bridgeman with just one hole to go. If he can shoot under par, Rai can take the lead.It could make for an exciting ending at the 2026 Par 3 Contest.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 1:50 PM CDTChris CwikThe 2026 Par 3 Contest is reaching its end. Harry Hall was the first player to finish Wednesday, shooting -2 for the event.While that’s a solid number, it’s unlikely Hall will pick up the win. Barring a massive collapse by some competitors ahead of Hall, he’s likely to settle in around the middle of the pack.With a hole to go, Aaron Rai leads the pack at -5. But Jacob Bridgeman is right on his tail.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 1:13 PM CDTChris CwikFor the second year in a row, Keegan Bradley managed a hole in one at the Par 3 Contest.Bradley managed the feat on the sixth hole last year. And followed that up with an ace on the eight hole Wednesday.In doing so, he became the first player in Par 3 Contest history to hit a hole-in-one in back-to-back years.Keegan Bradley becomes the first player in Par 3 Contest history to make a hole-in-one in back-to-back years. #themasters— The Masters (@TheMasters) April 8, 2026Earlier in the contest, Justin Thomas became just the fifth player to have go at least 10 years between aces at the event.Justin Thomas' last ace at the Par 3 Contest was in 2016. He is the fifth person ever to go at least 10 years between aces in the Par 3 Contest. He joins Craig Stadler (32 years, 1979 & 2011), Gary Player (23 years, 1993 & 2016), Luke List (19 years, 2005 & 2024) and Mike… https://t.co/Ibfd0XIiQc pic.twitter.com/sxr0shws6P— The Masters (@TheMasters) April 8, 2026Wed, April 8, 2026 at 12:37 PM CDTChris CwikAnother hole, another hole in one. This time, it was Keegan Bradley who got in on the action, sinking the ace on the eighth hole.That now makes three total aces at the 2026 Par 3 Contest. Justin Thomas started things off on the second hole of the day. Wyndham Clark got it done on the seventh hole.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 12:29 PM CDTChris CwikHow many aces will we see at the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday? Thanks to Wyndham Clark, we now have multiple aces at the event.Clark managed his hole in one on the seventh hole of the day.With the accomplishment, Clark joined Justin Thomas as the only two golfers to hit an ace at the event … so far.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 12:22 PM CDTChris CwikGary Player still has it. The 90-year-old sunk a deep birdie put in the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday, showing the skills that made him a three-time Masters champion.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 12:08 PM CDTChris CwikCam Smith wasn’t going to let a bad position sink his chances. With his ball in the sand, Smith managed to hit a birdie, taking a lead in the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday.Smith need to both get the ball out of the sand and avoid the lip of the grass with his shot. He navigated both issues perfectly to sink the birdie and take the lead.Smith is through five holes, so there’s still plenty of time left for the leaderboard to shift.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 11:49 AM CDTChris CwikThe Par 3 Contest is meant to be fun, and Scottie Scheffler decided to take advantage of that Wednesday.The Masters favorite decided to share a tender moment with his son Bennett just before hitting a ball off the tee.Both Scottie and Bennett lined up shots, with Bennett shooting it the wrong way.Scheffler is one of the many golfers not scoring at the event, so he’s just enjoying himself before the first round of the Masters tomorrow.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 11:38 AM CDTChris CwikIt’s still incredibly early, but José María Olazábal and Wyndham Clark hold the early lead at the Par 3 Contest. Both men sit at -1, though Olazábal has played one more hole so far.A number of competitors are no longer scoring at the event, cutting the field pretty low early on. That list includes Justin Thomas, who was at -2 through five holes after his early hole in one.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 11:21 AM CDTChris CwikWhat a start for Justin Thomas! On the second hole of the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday, Thomas picked up a hole in one.The shot was incredibly placed, as Thomas put just the right amount of spin on the ball to make it charge back into the hole after bouncing past it.Thomas may have had a little something on the line with his fellow competitors if his celebration was any indication.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 11:17 AM CDTKate MagdziukAn absolute legend on the ninth hole.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 11:14 AM CDTCaroline Fenton, Jason FitzWed, April 8, 2026 at 10:58 AM CDTYahoo Sports StaffScheffler heads into the 90th Masters as the favorite yet again at +600, but he is not among our picks to win … because that would be no fun.Here’s a look at which players our experts are picking to walk away with the coveted green jacket at the 2026 Masters Tournament:Jay Busbee: Bryson DeChambeau (+1200)Dan Wolken: Ludvig Åberg (+1400)Jay Hart: Jon Rahm (+1000)Ryan Young: Ludvig Åberg (+1400)Read more on why our experts made their picks here.Wed, April 8, 2026 at 10:45 AM CDTYahoo Sports StaffRound 1 of the 2026 Masters Tournament tees off on Thursday.
